Abstract:

The increasing demand for miniaturized and multifunctional devices has intensified research on&nbspmultiferroic materials due to their coupled ferroic properties. In this work, polycrystalline double&nbspperovskite NdYFe₂O₆ was synthesized for the first time using the sol-gel auto-combustion method.&nbspThe structural, magnetic, electrical, and magnetoelectric properties of samples sintered at 1000 &degC&nbspand 1200 &degC were systematically investigated. X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed the formation of&nbspthe desired crystalline double perovskite phase. Magnetic and electrical studies revealed the&nbspcoexistence of magnetic and electric order parameters within the material. The magnetoelectric&nbspcoupling behaviour demonstrated an interaction between the magnetic and electric subsystems. The&nbspobserved properties were found to be strongly influenced by the sintering temperature, highlighting&nbspthe role of microstructural evolution. These findings suggest that NdYFe₂O₆ is a promising
multifunctional material for future self-powered electronic devices and advanced energy efficient&nbspapplications.
